LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 6.31 WORD CLASS: DETERMINERS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.3: Grammar in Use 6.31 Word Class: Determiners

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Grammar in Use 6.31 Word Class: Determiners. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How can we quantify nouns we cannot count?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify quantifiers and nouns used with them appropriately for effective communication,
2. use quantifiers in sentences correctly for communication clarity,
3. adopt the correct use of quantifiers in everyday communication. The learner is guided to: from a list provided by the teacher, and any) correctly with nouns and construct sentences with peers, quantifiers (much, many, some and any) in small groups, quantifiers, poem or a paragraph featuring the quantifiers (much, many, some and any), and any) in a role-play or a dialogue with peers. SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Grammar in Use 6.31 Word Class: Determiners.
2. Explain Grammar in Use 6.31 Word Class: Determiners to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Try this activity: select countable and uncountable nouns from a list provided by the teacher,
4. Show that you can: identify quantifiers and nouns used with them appropriately for effective communication,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Grammar in Use 6.31 Word Class: Determiners. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: How can we quantify nouns we cannot count?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.
